Input Discussion: Implementation of Default Plugins for .zsh Background Currently, our dotfiles repository includes a basic .zsh configuration, but it lacks a standardized set of default plugins that would enhance productivity and provide a consistent development environment across team members. Proposal Implement a curated set of default plugins for .zsh that would be automatically loaded for all users of our dotfiles. This would include: 1. zsh-autosuggestions - Fish-like autosuggestions based on command history 2. zsh-syntax-highlighting - Command-line syntax highlighting 3. zsh-completions - Additional completion definitions 4. git - Git integration and aliases 5. docker - Docker completion and aliases (if relevant to our workflow) Implementation Considerations - Should plugins be managed via a plugin manager (zinit, antigen, etc.) or git submodules? - Should there be an opt-out mechanism for users who prefer minimal configurations? - How to handle plugin updates and version compatibility? - Should we include configuration for common tools we use (kubectl, terraform, etc.)? Questions for Discussion 1. Which plugin manager should we standardize on? 2. What other plugins would be valuable for our team? 3. How should we handle plugin configuration and customization? 4. Should this be part of the main dotfiles or a separate module? Please share your thoughts and suggestions on this implementation. into index 46.
